description.narrative: Scaling Social Impact, is a project which is taking place in India and will focus in particular on the Indian textile industry and within that, the jute supply chain in West Bengal. India is the second largest producer of textiles after China and the third largest exporter of textiles after China and Bangladesh. India is the biggest global cotton producer and accounts for 50% of global jute production. The textiles and apparel industry in India is the third largest employer in the country, providing direct employment to 45 million people and a larger unaccounted invisible informal workforce. 70 percent of the 45 million working women in India who work, work in the textile industry versus an overall female labour participation of only 28.3%. The textile industry is rife with poverty wages and low incomes, breaches of labour and human rights at work including the risk of child labour at farm and mill level. Research is done in partnership with Social Compact to identify whether and to what extent these issues are present in the supply chain and surrounding communities in project A. In project B the most salient risks will turn into opportunities for impact. Tiny Miracles creates a product to solve a problem: the project partners’ core motivation is to create social impact, not only for their own workers and their families and communities but also for the workers and communities in their supply chain. Rather than focusing on risk, Tiny Miracles wants to focus on scaling positive social impact by:a) Working with their suppliers to create social impact in our supply chain; andb) Creating a platform for organisations with a similar mission, but without the access to the market of multinational brands. Tiny Miracles will support social impact programs, salaries build-up, impact story telling, and product development. Bally Fabs International Limited, project partner and supplier, and part of the Kankaria group of Kolkata, India, has always invested heavily in corporate social responsibility (CSR), including provision of education, healthcare, financial support for the poor, farmer capacity building and food provision for the hungry through its charitable foundations. Partner and supplier Giriraj Nature Care Bags is interested to build on good practices, through learning and project activities.
